numberItems.stem: In stab braking, after you let off the brakes, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again?
numberItems.explanation: It can take up to 1 second for the wheels to start rolling; reapply before they roll and the vehicle won't straighten out. ½ second is brake lag (pp. 5-11–5-12).

numberItems.stem: How long is the brake lag on air brakes (the delay while air flows through the lines)?
numberItems.explanation: Air brakes take ½ second or more to work; hydraulic brakes are the ones that work instantly (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: With air brakes, how many parts make up total stopping distance?
options: 4: perception, reaction, brake lag and braking
4: perception, reaction, following distance and braking
numberItems.explanation: Air brakes add brake lag, so there are 4 parts: perception + reaction + brake lag + braking distance (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: At 55 mph on dry pavement, about how much distance does air brake lag add?
numberItems.explanation: Brake lag adds about 32 feet at 55 mph; in Figure 5.6, 61 ft is reaction distance and 216 ft is braking distance (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: An average driver with good traction and air brakes is going 55 mph. About how far does it take to stop?
numberItems.explanation: At 55 mph total stopping distance is over 450 feet (451 ft in Figure 5.6); 243 ft is at 35 mph and 346 ft at 45 mph (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: In the handbook's air brake stopping chart (Figure 5.6), what is the total stopping distance at 35 mph?
numberItems.explanation: Figure 5.6 totals: 15 mph 81 ft, 25 mph 155 ft, 35 mph 243 ft, 45 mph 346 ft, 55 mph 451 ft (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: Using the proper downhill braking technique, when do you release the brakes?
options: When you are about 5 mph above your "safe" speed
When you are about 5 mph below your "safe" speed
As soon as you reach your "safe" speed
numberItems.explanation: Brake at your safe speed until you are about 5 mph below it, then release; repeat when speed climbs back to the safe speed (p. 5-12).

numberItems.stem: In the proper downhill braking technique, each brake application should last about how long?
numberItems.explanation: Each application, from safe speed down to about 5 mph below it, should last about 3 seconds (p. 5-12).
